title: How to spot a scam open call or a vanity gallery
seoTitle: Art Open Call Scams: How to Check a Gallery Invitation
description: Red flags in art open calls and gallery invitations, a ten-minute check to run on any organizer before you pay, and what to do if you’ve already sent money.
summary: How to check an open call or gallery invitation before you pay: the red flags, a ten-minute check, and what to do if you’ve paid.
answer: Before you send money or work, check the organizer, the venue, how work is selected, the full cost and the written terms. Verify any unexpected invitation through contact details you find yourself. A paid show can be an honest service, but hidden charges, impersonation and pressure to pay are reasons to stop. A listing isn’t a guarantee.
keyPoints: Check unexpected invitations through the organization’s own website, never the links in the message.
A fee alone isn’t proof of a scam. Hidden costs, impersonation and pressure to pay are red flags.
If you’ve paid a scammer, save the evidence and contact your bank or card issuer quickly.
